claims.statement: langgraph.json registers the `chess` graph as the factory `apps/server/langchain_chess_server/graph.py:make_graph` and the custom HTTP app as `apps/server/langchain_chess_server/app.py:app`.

For a run (runtime.execution_runtime present), make_graph resolves ChessContext from both the run config and the ServerRuntime, then calls build_agent with a fresh ServerSettings; assistant context reaches the graph only through the runtime argument.

build_agent passes no chat model for policy `systemone`, uses NoSystemOne for policy `llm` and one SystemOneMiddleware for `systemone` and `hybrid`, always appends GameSetupMiddleware, forces memory to `none` when there is no model, and names the agent `chess` with ChessContext as context_schema.
Building the chess graph never calls a model or the System 1 classifier.

When policy is `systemone`, SystemOneMiddleware is built with threshold and tournament_threshold forced to 0.0 and has_model=False regardless of context, so System 1 always plays; for hybrid the context thresholds apply.
Each TypeSafeClassifier is built per graph build but takes its sync and async HTTP clients from a process-wide ClientPool (POOL, 15 second timeout), so all classifiers share one connection pair.

The server's chat_model delegates to langchain_chess.chat_models.chat_model, which calls init_chat_model with max_tokens set to an output budget (MAX_TOKENS 64000, capped by the model's output limit and half of a smaller window), a name set to the bare model name so gateway traces don't all read as ChatOpenAI, reasoning_effort only when set, and a profile whose max_input_tokens is the known context window minus the budget (gateway models the price snapshot doesn't know get no profile).

With a chat model and memory=`summarize`, build_agent raises a ChessContractError (telling the user to use memory='none') when the model has no known input limit in its profile; systemone with summarize still builds because memory is forced to none.

ChessContext defaults are policy `hybrid`, model `langsmith:baseten/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, reasoning_effort None, show_legal_moves True, memory `none` (only `none` or `summarize` allowed), systemone_model `semif-qwen3.5-4b`, style `rich`, with_eval and with_nouls False, gate `margin`, threshold 0.9, tournament_threshold None, k 5, top_p None, draw_claims `auto`, seed 0.
Each ChessContext knob carries json_schema_extra `langgraph_nodes` naming the nodes it affects so Studio can highlight them.

resolve_context starts from assistant context, drops unknown keys, overlays known keys from config configurable (configurable wins), lets an explicit None override only nullable knobs while omitted keys keep the assistant value, and validates the result with a pydantic TypeAdapter so bad values fail the run up front.

The web client sends exactly the ChessContext keys (derived from DEFAULT_CONTEXT) as configurable on every submit, and its ChessContext types and defaults in packages/chess-ui are hand-mirrored from the Python dataclass.
ServerSettings reads the shell then `.env`, rejects any of LANGSMITH_GATEWAY_API_KEY, TYPESAFE_API_KEY or TYPESAFE_BASE_URL that is set but blank, and holds no model credentials itself.
TypeSafe settings are required only when System 1 middleware is built: an llm-only graph builds without TYPESAFE_API_KEY while hybrid raises ValueError.
GET /ui/config returns the graph id `chess`, the ChessContext JSON schema, and the dataclass defaults.
The UI is mounted under /ui rather than / because custom routes shadow the Agent Server's own routes and / is its health check; /ui redirects to /ui/.
The static UI is mounted with app.mount and StaticFiles instead of app.frontend(), because frontend routes are low priority and the Agent Server's own /ui mount would answer first.
The static mount happens only when the Vite build directory exists (produced in CI before deploy); otherwise /ui/ returns a 404 JSON hint while /ui/config still answers.

model_limit builds the model through the same chat_model factory and returns its input limit, or None when the model has no known limit or cannot be built; it is exposed as GET /ui/model-limit, which requires a `model` query parameter, and the web client's fetchModelLimit maps the answer to known, none (null limit) or failed (request or body error) for the new-game dialog's decision whether to offer `summarize`.

When the Agent Server calls make_graph without an execution runtime (state reads, updates, graph introspection), it returns shape(): a chess graph with no model, NoSystemOne and a never-written GameSetupMiddleware, which needs no clients or credentials.

Every build of the chess graph has the same nodes regardless of settings: the llm policy uses NoSystemOne (named SystemOneMiddleware, same state schema, no-op hook), create_chess_agent is called with fixed_topology=True so a no-op summarization node remains under memory='none', and GameSetupMiddleware is always present; tests assert run and read graphs have identical topology for every policy and memory.

ClientPool creates its client pair lazily under a lock so concurrent first uses make one pair, and aclose closes the pair so the next get makes a fresh one; the FastAPI app's lifespan (merged by the Agent Server with its own) calls POOL.aclose on shutdown.

The client pool lives in its own module imported by package name because langgraph loads graph.py by file path under a generated module name; a pool kept in graph.py would exist once per copy, and a test checks that shutdown closes the clients of a path-loaded graph.py.
ChessContext numeric knobs are bounded and validated at resolution: threshold and tournament_threshold in [0, 1], k from 1 to CHOICE_LIMIT (255), top_p in (0, 1].

GameSetupMiddleware writes a `setup` state key holding asdict of the run's resolved ChessContext only on the game's first turn (no existing setup, exactly one turn, opened by this run), in both before_agent and after_agent; later runs never overwrite it, a failed first turn still records it, a rejected first input records none, and threads from before setup existed never gain one.
The web client continues a game from its thread by reading `setup` through recordedContext, which accepts it only when every knob is present and valid rather than filling in defaults.
